shared: Redesign this game's sprite art for MUCH clearer small-screen readability while strictly KEEPING THE PIXEL-ART medium and the existing warm fantasy-industrial world. This MUST look like carefully hand-pixelled 16-bit isometric game sprites, with obvious stair-step pixel silhouettes, dark teal pixel outlines, large tidy hand-placed pixel clusters and hard 2-3 tone pixel shading. Think a 64x64 logical-pixel sprite, integer upscaled, with only a few broad color groups. NOT smooth 3D, NOT vector, NOT glossy toy rendering, NOT anti-aliased cartoon illustration. Reduce tiny detail by about 75 percent. Eliminate busy material grain, dithering, many tiny roof tiles, dozens of outlines, minute brickwork, straps, nails and scattered accessories. Simplify geometry and interior linework, not by blurring. Preserve a charming mature pixel-game style. Transparent background, no people, no text or labels. Production atlas: EXACTLY 4 columns by 4 rows in equal square cells with 15 percent clear padding on all four sides of each sprite including smoke. 4 rows are the SAME facility seen from SE/front+right, NE/back+right, NW/back+left, SW/front+left; fixed orthographic 35.264-degree elevation and real 90-degree view changes. 4 columns are states of identical architecture. Keep constant footprint, scale and ground anchor across all frames. All pixels belong within their own cells. Thin footprint only, no thick floating tile.  CRITICAL GAME GRID CONSTRAINT: the physical footprint is exactly ONE SQUARE TILE, equal world width and world depth 1:1, NEVER a long rectangular site. Every sprite stands on the same thin compact square foundation pad, projected as a diamond from the fixed isometric camera. The diamond has width:height approximately 1.73:1 on screen, because the actual footprint is square viewed from above at 35.264 degrees. Its four vertices are consistent in every frame: left/right corners at the same screen height, centered top and bottom corners. Foundation pad centered horizontally, identical width/depth and screen baseline throughout atlas. Object occupies 75-80% of this square pad with 10% clear inset on every WORLD side; all crates, logs, buckets and output planks remain INSIDE this one square. No overhanging accessory piles or rectangular elongated buildings. A single low muted stone rim around the foundation is allowed to make the SQUARE footprint clear; no grass decoration, no thick block. The art can rise vertically over the pad; keep foundation projected correctly rather than forcing the whole building into a flat diamond.

subjects.warehouse: SQUARE-FOOTPRINT WAREHOUSE: a compact honey-wood shed with EQUAL LENGTH FRONT AND SIDE WALLS in world space. Neither wall is longer than the other. Medium-height block with a dark-teal gable roof, represented as two broad pixel-shaded planes with just TWO wide roof seams. Very large double cargo doors cover most of front wall; ONE large simple X-braced shipping crate tucked into the pad's front corner, INSIDE the same square tile footprint. No sacks or decorative piles. Keep building front and side approximately equally visible in SE view, not a wide front and narrow side. Columns doors closed, half open, fully open with one box inside, half closing. In rear views show plain closed rear wall with a broad vent and unchanged states. Strong hand-pixelled identity of supplied style reference; simplify as before, but redraw the rectangular reference into a genuine square-base facility. Approximately 12-16 intentional colors, no 3D/cartoon/vector conversion.
subjects.house: RESIDENT HOME. Small cream-plaster cube, simple muted terracotta-red pixel gable roof made of large clean clusters with no tile pattern, ONE broad yellow window and one wooden front door, one chunky stone chimney. No dormer, exposed timber crossbeams, flowerpots, firewood stack, tiny trim or masonry noise. Retain hand-pixelled dark outlines and honey/cream/teal-shadow color family of the game's art. Four states: no smoke, one small chunky grey pixel smoke puff just above actual chimney, two rising pixel puffs, two fading pixel puffs. Smoke always comes directly from actual chimney in each view, within cell. Distinct HOME silhouette at 48px.
subjects.well: WATER WELL. Exposed very readable bright turquoise water inside one low 8-sided grey stone ring, just TWO honey-wood posts and a straight crossbar supporting a large blue-grey bucket. NO canopy roof: make water and bucket the largest identifying features. Ring has just four to six broad stone blocks. No second bucket, ground debris, detailed crank or brick texture. Hand-pixelled clusters and dark pixel outline consistent with supplied warehouse style. State columns: bucket parked at rim, bucket lowered into water with long straight rope, bucket half raised with short rope, bucket up with two BIG pixel water drops. Only bucket and rope move, stone ring/posts remain exactly fixed. Four true 90-degree views.
subjects.lumber: LOGGING CAMP. An open short honey-wood rack holding TWO LARGE dark-brown round logs with huge tan circular end faces. ONE large SILVER AXE with muted GREEN handle planted in one chunky chopping stump beside the rack. NO roof, crane, tall derrick, pulley ropes, fine grain or scattered wood chips. Logs and axe are the clear silhouette and visual function. A simple hand-lever at side and the upper log resting on two small supports. Animation columns: two logs at rest; top log rolls a short distance on support; top log further along support; top log back slightly. Keep the axe planted, stump and rack identical; no floating tools. Pixel art with blocky curves, broad 2-tone clusters, dark teal/brown pixel outlines and same palette family. Four real camera views, axes/logs stay at consistent world locations. Both logs are SHORT and thick, ending well before the pad boundary. Keep stump and axe on this same square pad. No long rectangular logging yard.
subjects.field: WHEAT FIELD. A very thin brown isometric square soil patch with exactly THREE tidy planting rows and NO irrigation channel or tub. Only NINE plants maximum, 3 by 3 with generous exposed brown soil between. Four growth columns: three broad tilled rows; nine tiny 2-leaf green sprouts; nine knee-height green wheat plants; nine chunky golden wheat heads each made of 3-5 large pixel clusters above dark-green stems. Remove fine stalks, seed dots, gritty earth, weeds and all microtexture. Same footprint throughout, all 4 row directions rotate crop-row orientation logically. Clearly intentional 16-bit pixel art, not a smooth vector icon or 3D rendering. At 48px the golden crop rows should remain clearly separated. The soil diamond is itself the single SQUARE 1x1 foundation, no stone platform underneath. Its vertices follow the same camera projection as other facilities.
subjects.sawmill: SAWMILL. A compact open honey-wood bench with NO shed, NO roof, NO chimney. ONE oversized upright silver circular SAW BLADE with 8 big pixel teeth on a dark-teal machine housing, one thick brown round input log at one side, exactly THREE broad pale-yellow straight finished planks at output side. One plain broad orange drive wheel on side. Log -> blade -> planks must read instantly at 48px. Blade always visible from each view, logs visibly ROUND and output boards RECTANGULAR. No pipes, belts, bolts, beams everywhere, scraps or detailed wood grain. Strong dark pixel outlines, coarse silver/honey/teal pixel clusters, limited palette. Four state columns: idle log before blade, log feeds through with blade rotation, log advanced and blade rotated, output boards slightly advanced. Keep machine architecture and screen footprint fixed; change only blade/feed/boards. The workbench is compact and nearly SQUARE, with SHORT log and SHORT three output boards all fully inside the same square pad. No long conveyor or rectangular site.
